A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same TimeFormer research work. All 14 pages, including equations, figures, tables, algorithms and Appendices A–D, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on N3DV, HyperNeRF and NeRF-DS, with quantitative comparisons, qualitative examples and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including Tables 1–6 and the supplementary canonical-space, rendering-speed and ablation results.

M1.justification: The Cross-Temporal Encoder, shared deformation fields, two-stream training losses and removal of TimeFormer during inference are unchanged. Appendix A's Algorithms 1–2 also match.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same scenes and tasks: multi-view reconstruction on N3DV, monocular reconstruction on HyperNeRF and dynamic specular objects on NeRF-DS. No additional coverage appears in the appendices.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 3 and 4 retain exactly the same comparator rows in their corresponding experiments, including the distinct GS4D [68] and 4DGS [61] entries in Table 1. No comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: The reported settings and procedures match, including B=4, M=4, loss weights, PSNR/SSIM evaluation, LPIPS in ablations and random versus continuous timestamp sampling. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix D retain the same batch-size, sampling, encoder-depth and weight-sharing ablations. Temporal PSNR, convergence, motion visualization and canonical-space/FPS analyses also match, including supplementary Figures 12–13.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates and scene averages. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 retains mean PSNR of 31.10/31.84 for 4DGS without/with TimeFormer and 31.62/32.23 for STGS. Tables 2–6 and the supplementary figure results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The Gaussian definitions, rendering and deformation equations, gradient derivation in Equations 6–9 and losses in Equations 10–12 are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: plug-and-play temporal modeling, two-stream knowledge transfer, improved reconstruction and inference without the auxiliary module.

C2.justification: Both versions give the same explanations involving cross-time attention, faster optimization and more efficient Gaussian distributions. The limitation concerning overly smooth textures on intricately detailed objects is also unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix A retain the same A100 hardware disclosure, hyperparameters, pseudocode and implementation explanations. Training-time reports, the project-page link and Appendix C's demo access instructions are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research-positioning passages and all 74 reference entries match. No cited work or substantive relationship to prior research is added or revised.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 18 November 2024 to v2 dated 6 October 2025. The title, author text, prose, section organization and Appendices A–D remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–13, Tables 1–6 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same content, captions, structures and placement. Tiny character-position differences from PDF rendering do not alter the page layout or scientific displays.

improvement.justification: The complete main text and appendices retain the same scientific content, evidence, explanations, limitations and reproducibility information. The updated arXiv stamp and negligible rendering differences provide no meaningful gain or loss in overall paper quality.
